message.content: Trade helped the pharaoh, and he used its wealth to strengthen his rule. You can see that in his army, his temples, and his courts. We know that it moved gold, ivory, timber, and grain, so they gained rare goods. The king controlled the routes, and he collected their profits; he also paid his officials, his soldiers, and his workers. You may ask why that mattered, and it did, because it made him look more powerful. They obeyed him, and he rewarded them with land, food, and status. We should note that it connected Egypt to Nubia, Asia, and the sea, so he could show his strength to foreign rulers. You should understand that it enriched the court, strengthened the army, and made the throne seem stable. In short, he relied on it, and it helped him keep power.
